text: So over time, a word can come to mean something that is beyond what that actual word means. Like Disney means magic today. Volvo means safety. Those names are not good.
speaker: Arielle Jackson
context: Lenny is asking Arielle about the importance of company names and whether a bad name can hurt a startup. Arielle explains that while a great name can help with word-of-mouth and memorability, a bad name won't necessarily doom a good company with strong strategy and marketing. She uses Disney and Volvo as examples - names that weren't inherently good but became powerful through consistent branding over time, with Disney now meaning 'magic' and Volvo representing 'safety.'
text_ko: 시간이 지나면 어떤 단어가 원래 의미를 넘어서 다른 의미를 갖게 될 수 있어요. 예를 들어 지금 디즈니는 ‘마법’을, 볼보는 ‘안전’을 의미해요. 그런 이름들은 별로 좋지 않아요.
text_zh: 时间长了，一个词就能超越它本身的意思，变成别的含义。比如迪士尼现在就代表魔法，沃尔沃就等于安全。但这些名字本身其实都不怎么样。
text_es: Con el tiempo, una palabra puede llegar a significar algo que va más allá de lo que realmente significa esa palabra. Como Disney hoy en día significa magia. Volvo significa seguridad. Esos nombres no están bien.
key_sentence: over time, a word can come to mean something that is beyond what that actual word means.
original_text: So over time, a word can come to mean something that is beyond what that actual word means. Like Disney means magic today. Volvo means safety. Those names are not good. If I just put it in a spreadsheet or one of those lists, no one would pick it. So that's kind of what I mean, that the name is just part of the overall marketing or the overall brand and a bad name with a really great company with great company strategy, great marketing is going to be great over time. And a good name is just going to help you, but I don't think a bad name is going to kill a good company.

vocabulary.definition: At or to the further side of; outside the limits of something. It can also imply surpassing a particular threshold or expectation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'beyond' is often used to describe goals or achievements that exceed standard expectations, such as 'beyond profit' to indicate a focus on sustainability.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can convey a sense of aspiration or ambition, but may also imply that something is unattainable or overly idealistic.

text: And I personally tend to like those kinds of names that are suggestive or evocative, where when I tell you what the company does, you're like, oh, that makes sense. But it's not that what the name is tells you exactly what the company does.
speaker: Arielle Jackson
context: Lenny asks Arielle what makes a good name for a startup or product. Arielle explains her preference for suggestive or evocative names - names that make sense once you understand what the company does, but don't literally describe the service. She uses Maven as an example, explaining how the Yiddish word meaning 'one who understands through experience' perfectly fits a platform where experienced operators teach cohort-based classes to others.
text_ko: 저는 개인적으로 회사가 뭘 하는지 말해주면 '아, 그럴 만하네요' 하고 납득이 가는, 연상시키거나 분위기를 풍기는 이름을 좋아해요. 다만 그 이름만으로 회사가 정확히 뭘 하는지는 알 수는 없어요.
text_zh: 我个人比较喜欢那种有暗示性的名字，就是当我告诉你这家公司是做什么的时候，你会恍然大悟"哦，原来如此"。但这个名字本身不会直接告诉你公司具体做什么业务。
text_es: Y a mí personalmente me gustan ese tipo de nombres que sugieren algo o te evocan una idea, donde cuando te explico a qué se dedica la empresa, dices "ah, tiene sentido". Pero no es que el nombre te diga exactamente qué hace la empresa.
key_sentence: those kinds of names that are suggestive or evocative, where when I tell you what the company does, you're like, oh, that makes sense.
original_text: And I personally tend to like those kinds of names that are suggestive or evocative, where when I tell you what the company does, you're like, oh, that makes sense. But it's not that what the name is tells you exactly what the company does. Another company that has a good name that you and I have both worked with is Maven. Maven is a Yiddish word that means one who understands and it means specifically one who understands because they've done something, they've acquired the skills or knowledge over time. And I just think that's such a cool name for a platform that allows X operators or current operators to teach their skills to other people through cohort based classes.

vocabulary.definition: Implying or indicating something indirectly; often used to describe names or terms that hint at a deeper meaning or association.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, suggestive names can enhance brand identity by evoking certain feelings or associations that resonate with consumers.
vocabulary.nuance: While suggestive terms can be powerful in branding, they may also risk ambiguity if the implication is not clear to the target audience.

vocabulary.definition: Bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind; often used to describe language or branding that stirs emotional responses.
vocabulary.businessContext: Evocative branding can create a strong emotional connection with consumers, enhancing brand loyalty and recognition.
vocabulary.nuance: Evocative terms are effective in marketing but should be used carefully to ensure they align with the brand's message and values.

vocabulary.definition: To be logical or reasonable; often used to indicate that something is understandable or coherent.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, saying something 'makes sense' can validate a proposal or idea, indicating that it aligns with common understanding or expectations.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase can imply agreement or approval, but may also suggest that the alternative lacks clarity or rationale.

vocabulary.definition: In a precise manner; used to indicate that something is accurate or corresponds precisely to a description or expectation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, 'exactly' is often used to affirm understanding or agreement on specific details or requirements.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'exactly' conveys precision, overuse can come across as pedantic or overly critical in collaborative discussions.

text: My take on empty vessel names is they can be really memorable and they can be evocative of the emotion, but you have to do a lot more marketing work over time to make it mean something.
speaker: Arielle Jackson
context: Lenny asks about nonsense words as company names like Yahoo and Google. Arielle explains the concept of 'empty vessel names' - names that don't have inherent meaning but can become powerful brand assets. However, she warns that these names require significantly more marketing investment and time to build meaning, using Yahoo as an example of how much effort was needed to make that meaningless word represent a search engine in people's minds.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 내용이 담기지 않은 이름(empty vessel names)은 기억에 잘 남고 감성적으로도 와닿을 수 있어요. 다만 그 이름에 의미를 부여하려면 시간이 흐르면서 훨씬 더 많은 마케팅 작업을 해야 해요.
text_zh: 我觉得那些空泛的名字吧，确实容易让人记住，也能勾起一些情感共鸣，但问题在于你得花大量的营销功夫才能让它真正有意义。
text_es: Mi opinión sobre los nombres de marca abstractos es que pueden ser súper memorables y despertar emociones, pero te va a tocar hacer mucho más trabajo de marketing con el tiempo para que realmente signifiquen algo.
key_sentence: Empty vessel names require more marketing work to become evocative of the emotion.
original_text: My take on empty vessel names is they can be really memorable and they can be evocative of the emotion, but you have to do a lot more marketing work over time to make it mean something. So if I say Yahoo today, we know it's that search engine we use before we all switch to Google and we have the purple color in our head, and we think about what it meant at the time that we might have used it, but it took a lot of marketing dollars and a lot of time for that word to be in that.

vocabulary.definition: Easily remembered or recalled; having qualities that make it stand out in one's memory.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, creating memorable branding or marketing campaigns can significantly enhance customer recognition and loyalty.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'memorable' often has a positive connotation, it can also imply that something is overly simplistic or gimmicky if not executed well.

vocabulary.definition: Bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind; capable of eliciting emotional responses.
vocabulary.businessContext: Evocative advertising aims to create an emotional connection with consumers, often leading to stronger brand loyalty and engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'evocative' is typically used in a positive sense, but it can also suggest that the emotional appeal may overshadow the product's actual qualities.

vocabulary.definition: The activities and strategies employed to promote and sell products or services to consumers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, effective marketing work is essential for building brand awareness, attracting customers, and driving sales.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase 'marketing work' can imply a significant investment of time and resources, often requiring ongoing efforts to maintain market presence.

text: Almost always when someone comes to me and says, I'm ready to announce, we go back to positioning first.
speaker: Arielle Jackson
context: Lenny asks Arielle for tactical advice on getting PR for startups before launch. Arielle emphasizes that founders often rush to announce without proper preparation. She stresses the importance of having clear positioning first, ensuring your website can handle traffic, and having realistic expectations about which media outlets will actually cover an early-stage startup and how long the PR process takes.
text_ko: 거의 항상 누군가가 저에게 "이제 발표할 준비가 됐어요"라고 말하면, 저희는 먼저 포지셔닝(positioning)으로 다시 돌아가요.
text_zh: 几乎每次有人跟我说"我准备发布了"的时候，我们都得先回头把定位(positioning)的问题搞清楚。
text_es: Casi siempre cuando alguien viene y me dice "ya estoy listo para hacer el anuncio", volvemos primero al tema del posicionamiento.
key_sentence: we go back to positioning first.
original_text: Almost always when someone comes to me and says, I'm ready to announce, we go back to positioning first. Also make sure that your website is ready for the traffic you're going to drive to it, that you're not driving traffic to a name that you're going to later scrap. Are you really ready for this? So go back to all the other things we discussed first and then having realistic expectations about the outlets that will cover you and the time it will take to get them.

vocabulary.definition: The strategic process of establishing a brand or product in the minds of consumers relative to competitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, effective positioning helps to differentiate a product or service in the market, guiding marketing strategies and customer perceptions.
vocabulary.nuance: Positioning often implies a long-term strategy and can involve complex market analysis; it is not merely about immediate sales tactics.

vocabulary.definition: To make a public declaration about something, typically to inform stakeholders or the general public.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, announcements can pertain to product launches, company news, or changes in leadership, and are crucial for maintaining transparency and engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a formal tone and is often used in contexts where clarity and authority are required; it is less appropriate for informal communications.

text: These days for early stage startups, we're almost always running the launch announcement as an exclusive, which means you give the news to a single outlet. And they're the only ones who get to write about it.
speaker: Arielle Jackson
context: Arielle is explaining how PR strategy has evolved for early-stage startups. She describes how the traditional approach of briefing multiple outlets under embargo no longer works effectively. Instead, modern startup PR typically involves giving exclusive coverage rights to a single media outlet, while still allowing the company to use their own channels (blog, social media, investor updates) to share the news.
text_ko: 요즘 초기 스타트업(early-stage startups)들은 거의 항상 런칭 발표(launch announcement)를 단독(exclusive)으로 진행해요. 즉 소식은 한 매체(outlet)에만 제공하고 그 매체만 보도하게 해요.
text_zh: 现在对于早期创业公司来说，我们发布产品时基本都是找一家媒体独家报道，就是说你只给一个媒体平台爆料，只有他们能写这个消息。
text_es: Hoy en día para las startups en etapa temprana, casi siempre manejamos el anuncio de lanzamiento como exclusiva, o sea que le das la noticia a un solo medio. Y son los únicos que pueden escribir sobre eso.
key_sentence: We're running the launch announcement as an exclusive for a single outlet.
original_text: These days for early stage startups, we're almost always running the launch announcement as an exclusive, which means you give the news to a single outlet. And they're the only ones who get to write about it. You can obviously still do all your owned and operated stuff, your blog, your social, your investors, your friends and family, but they're the only like news outlet who gets to write about it.

vocabulary.definition: Limited to a single entity or group; not shared with others.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in media and marketing, an exclusive often refers to a situation where a company provides information or a product to only one media outlet or partner, enhancing its value and appeal.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a connotation of prestige and selectivity, often used to create a sense of urgency or importance around a product or announcement.

vocabulary.definition: A formal communication that introduces a new product, service, or initiative to the public or specific stakeholders.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, a launch announcement is critical for generating buzz and attracting attention from potential customers, investors, and the media.
vocabulary.nuance: This term implies a strategic moment in a company's timeline, often accompanied by marketing efforts to maximize visibility and impact.

text: Make what you do interesting and relevant... to all the readers... We turned all of our customers into heroes and went after local press... they are the ones hungry for these stories more than the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal.
speaker: Arielle Jackson
context: Arielle is providing PR advice about making startup stories newsworthy to journalists and their audiences. She explains that founders need to think beyond their own perspective and create stories that appeal to broader readerships. She shares a strategy from her Square days of making customers the heroes of stories and targeting local press, which is often more accessible and eager for startup stories than major national publications.
text_ko: 하시는 일을 모든 독자에게 흥미롭고 관련성 있게 만드세요. 저희는 모든 고객을 영웅으로 만들고 지역 언론(local press)을 적극적으로 공략했어요. 오히려 지역 언론이 이런 이야기를 뉴욕타임스나 월스트리트저널보다 더 원해요.
text_zh: 把你做的事情搞得有意思、有价值...对所有读者来说都是这样...我们把客户都包装成英雄人物，然后去找当地媒体...他们比《纽约时报》和《华尔街日报》更渴望这种故事。
text_es: Haz que lo que haces sea interesante y relevante... para todos los lectores... Convertimos a todos nuestros clientes en héroes y fuimos a por la prensa local... ellos son los que están más hambrientos de estas historias que el New York Times y el Wall Street Journal.
key_sentence: We turned all of our customers into heroes to attract local press hungry for stories.
original_text: The last thing is really about making what you do interesting and relevant so that it's not just interesting and relevant to you and the three other people who worked there at the time, but interesting to all the readers of whatever outlet you're trying to target. We turned all of our customers into heroes and went after local press. Most PR firms that service the tech community aren't experts in local press, but if you have a way to make some connections with some local press, they are the ones hungry for these stories more than the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal.

vocabulary.definition: Closely connected or appropriate to the matter at hand.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, ensuring that content, products, or services are relevant to target audiences is crucial for engagement and success.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'relevant' implies a direct connection, it is important to ensure that it aligns with the interests and needs of the audience to avoid being perceived as superficial.
